**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore the documented 60-project Pro limit**

The linked [Vercel limits table](https://vercel.com/docs/limits) currently caps **Vercel Projects Connected per Git Repository** at 60 for Pro, not 150. Leaving 150 here overstates how far a monorepo can scale before it must split across repositories or teams; restore 60 or avoid hard-coding the value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

DISAGREE: https://vercel.com/docs/limits (last_updated 2026-09-16) lists "Vercel Projects Connected per Git Repository | 25 | 150 | Custom" for Hobby / Pro / Enterprise, and the page links the changelog entry "Increased limit for projects per Git repo". 150 is the current Pro value; 60 is the previous one.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync the corrected outlier delta across the docs**

This correction to 37s matches the raw wall times (107.528s − 70.392s), but `bench/turbopack-gym/cache-drift.md:89` still describes the same run as only 33s longer. Update the companion methodology note too so the two records do not publish contradictory deltas for the same samples.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L1404-L1406](https://github.com/ejc3/node-monorepo-perf/blob/aea05233624088fca3a6ec451c2deb12c283747b/AGENTS.md#L1404-L1406)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

NOT-A-DEFECT: documentation correction, fixed in d383b12. bench/turbopack-gym/cache-drift.md now states both reps (107.5s with 71s after run-turbopack, vs 70.4s with 33s after) and the 37s difference, matching TURBOPACK-GRAPH.md and bench/turbopack-graph-drift.json (wall 107.528 vs 70.392). `node scripts/turbopack-gym/report.mjs --check` passes.

**🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Correct the Pro project-per-repository limit.**

`LIMITS.md` states that Pro allows 150 projects per repository. Vercel's limits page lists 60 projects connected per Git repository for Pro. Replace `150` with `60`; otherwise, readers will underestimate the repository count required for this deployment model. ([vercel.com](https://vercel.com/docs/limits?utm_source=openai))

# Limits and Gotchas at 20k Apps

## Irreducible Limits at 20k

7. **Deploy-platform per-project model.** One Vercel project per app, but Vercel caps projects per repo (Pro: 60; [Vercel limits](https://vercel.com/docs/limits)), so 20k apps split across repos/teams — itself a sharding pressure. Vercel's native "skip unaffected projects" does not consume a concurrent build slot; the deprecated `turbo-ignore` Ignored Build Step does. Use `turbo run --affected` plus the native skip.
